cues.text: You're early. I haven't even switched the front lights on.
Six meant six. I didn't want you waiting for me.
I wasn't expecting new shoes. Those look properly dry, anyway.
The shop had one pair left that actually fit me.
Good. You can leave your coat on for a minute.
Is that notice on the counter meant for the window?
I hadn't decided where it ought to go just yet.
It says permanently. That's quite a word to leave out.
I know what it says. I had it printed myself.
Then should I have called before coming down this morning?
No. You came when I asked you. You did right.
I thought the first thing would be learning the till.
We can leave the till alone until we've had coffee.
This one's empty. Were you going to make some now?
I was going to ask if you still take milk.
I do, but coffee isn't why I came here today.
I didn't say it was. Please give me a minute.
Was that notice printed before you offered me the job?
Yes. It was already here when we talked that night.
Then I need you to explain what I'm here for.
All right. Let's sit where we can actually hear ourselves.
I thought we'd sit a while before doing anything else.
You could have asked me for breakfast instead of work.
You might not have come if I'd called it breakfast.
You don't know that. You never gave me that choice.
No. I didn't. I thought I was making it easier.
Easier for which of us? I'm honestly asking you that.
For me, probably. I didn't want another morning here alone.
So this was supposed to be your last morning here?
One proper morning. Before I put that thing on display.
And I was supposed to sit here while you closed?
I hadn't worked out what I'd say when you arrived.
You told me six. I spent the night planning around it.
I meant that part. I wanted you to be here.
Being here isn't the same as having somewhere to work.
No. It isn't. I should have said what was happening.
I can hear bad news. I can't plan around guesses.
Then ask me what you need to know. I'll answer.
Is there any work here that you actually need done?
There is plenty. I just can't promise where it leads.
I'm asking about this morning. Start with what's actually here.
The counter needs setting. We can start with that much.
Only this end first. The other stools can stay empty.
How many places do you normally set before opening up?
All eight, usually. Then the booths, if I have time.
You said this end. Does that mean two places today?
Two is enough for now. I keep forgetting that part.
Do the handles face the person or face the till?
The person, unless they're left handed and move it themselves.
Good. That's something I can check without guessing your mind.
You'll have to ask things. I haven't trained anyone lately.
I can ask. Will you tell me when something matters?
Yes. And when it doesn't, I'll try to say that.
Are these two clean, or are they waiting for washing?
Clean. The dirty ones stay in the tray behind me.
Separate trays would help me keep the two things straight.
There used to be one. It cracked a while back.
Could an empty shelf do until you replace the tray?
The lower shelf is free. Don't put anything hot there.
I'll leave this here, away from the clean cup spaces.
That's sensible. I usually end up looking for the thing.
Then that can be my first job. Keeping this end ready.
It won't take three hours to put two mugs out.
Then tell me the next job when this one's done.
Before we do another job, we need to discuss pay.
I was going to get to that. Fifteen an hour.
For how many hours today, including the time we're talking?
Six until nine. Forty five dollars for the whole morning.
And that's work, even if nobody comes through the door?
Of course it is. You came here because I asked.
Can you pay that today, without using tomorrow's takings first?
Yes. Today's money is already separate from the bill money.
I need to ask. I've worked places that answered differently.
You don't need to explain why you want paying, Sam.
Then don't make that face when I ask about it.
What face? I'm trying to remember where I put things.
All right. I don't like admitting how little is certain.
I don't need everything certain. I need today's part clear.
Today is paid. Tomorrow is something we haven't agreed yet.
If today goes well, would there actually be another shift?
I don't know yet. I'm sorry, but that's the answer.
I'll write today down. I won't write tomorrow in yet.
That sounds fair. You can stop at nine without asking.
If you're behind, I still stop unless we agree otherwise?
Yes. I won't keep you here by looking worn out.
Good. Then we can talk about the work without guessing.
You haven't asked whether this changes what we discussed before.
I've been trying to keep those things apart this morning.
I told you to buy shoes. I meant that, Sam.
I did. But the rest of that money is mine?
Yes. It isn't a deposit on keeping this place open.
I needed you to say that without me offering first.
Were you going to offer? Please don't tell me yes.
I thought about it when I saw the closed notice.
Then I gave you the wrong idea by hiding things.
You made it hard to know what you actually wanted.
I wanted someone here. I should have asked you plainly.
I can come for breakfast without buying part of your problems.
You can. And you can take another job without asking.
Even if you teach me things and this goes badly?
Yes. Teaching you doesn't make your next decision belong here.
I don't want every mistake measured against what happened then.
Neither do I. But money mistakes will still need explaining.
That's fair, if you ask before deciding what I meant.
I'll ask. You tell me straight, even when you're embarrassed.
I can do that better if the answer isn't already chosen.
Then we'll both have something to practise while we're here.
All right. My savings stay separate. So does this job.
What made you print the notice instead of asking for help?
I asked in little ways. Nobody knew what I meant.
You could have said the cook leaving changes the hours.
I kept thinking I'd manage until I found somebody else.
Was there somebody else coming, or were you just hoping?
Just hoping. Then I started leaving jobs for the next morning.
I can still do the work. I can't do all of it.
Which part makes you want to turn round at the door?
Opening everything when I know I'll be closing everything alone.
Then maybe everything is too much to open this week.
People expect the booths, the hot food, all of it.
You don't have to promise every usual thing before breakfast.
I don't want them walking in and thinking we've given up.
They might think you changed the hours because you needed to.
You make it sound simple. I know it won't be.
I'm saying smaller. You can still tell me it's hard.
I wanted that notice to make the decision for me.
Do you want to close, if you can choose again?
I want to stop doing mornings that leave me flattened.
That's different. What would a morning you could manage look like?
One counter. Short hours. And somebody telling me to stop.
Let's work out that morning before we decide about forever.
Coffee and toast first. That's what I could manage myself.
Can you manage both while showing me what to do?
If you handle the clean cups and keep this counter clear.
I haven't worked the machine. I shouldn't guess with that.
You won't. I do the hot things until you've learned.
And if somebody asks me for something we aren't serving?
Tell them the choices. If they're unhappy, you call me.
You won't change your mind and start the whole kitchen?
I might want to. You'll probably see it on my face.
Then give me something definite I can remind you of.
No breakfast plates this week. Just the things we agreed.
Do we leave the booths closed, even if they're empty?
Yes. Four counter seats, so I can see what's happening.
You said two places earlier. Are we changing that already?
You're right. Two first. We can discuss four another day.
I'm not trying to catch you. I need instructions that hold.
Then two seats hold. I can live with two seats.
We should put the short menu somewhere people can read.
I'll explain it before they sit. That's my job today.
And I keep this bit ready without promising anything extra.
Exactly. If we're slow, we say we're slow, without excuses.
I can say that. I don't want to invent answers.
Neither do I. We can leave the bigger menu put away.
If we're discussing a week, I need numbers for that.
Five mornings, three hours each. Nothing on the weekend yet.
That's fifteen hours. At fifteen, you'd need two hundred twenty five.
I have that much set aside. It includes today's forty five.
Is that money needed for a bill that's due tomorrow?
Not tomorrow. The rent is the bill I'm worried about.
Would paying me mean you can't pay the rent afterward?
The rent was a problem before you walked in here.
That doesn't answer whether a week makes the problem worse.
It costs money. Staying shut also costs money every day.
I don't want you calling my wages another favour later.
They aren't a favour. They're the cost of asking you here.
Then keep the full week separate before we call it agreed.
That's reasonable. But I can't reserve another week behind it.
I'm not asking for another week. I'm asking about this one.
Two hundred twenty five. Paid each morning, not after Friday.
If we stop early, we settle the hours already worked?
Yes. And if I cancel, I tell you before you travel.
Before I leave home. That matters more than it sounds.
All right. Before you leave home. We choose a time.
Don't promise now if you need to check your figures.
I checked them last night. The wage money is there.
Then that's the limit. We don't cover gaps with my savings.
You'll make mistakes. I need to say that before we start.
I know. I don't know which ones you expect first.
Probably putting things where I can't find them at first.
If you haven't shown me, tell me where they belong.
Fair. And if I've shown you, ask me again anyway.
Suppose I put that cup in the wrong place twice?
Then we mark the shelf, instead of having an argument.
And if you change the place halfway through the morning?
I tell you first. You don't have to notice everything.
If the till is short, we check the numbers together?
Yes. Neither of us starts by deciding who to blame.
I don't want access to it until I've been shown.
You won't have to use it today. I handle payments.
If something breaks, I tell you before trying a repair.
Please do. I'm attached to several very unreliable old things.
And if a job feels unsafe, I can say no?
Yes. Then we find another way or leave it undone.
That includes carrying anything heavy because you're too tired, right?
It does. Asking for help doesn't mean ordering you about.
I can work hard. I just need to know the difference.
If I forget, remind me without waiting until you're furious.
I'll try. You might have to hear it twice sometimes.
That's all right. I haven't learned this part properly either.
I need a minute before I say yes to anything.
Take it. You don't have to answer while I'm watching.
I'm not trying to make you ask me twice, Ruth.
I know. I gave you rather more than you expected.
I thought I'd be nervous about remembering orders this morning.
I thought I'd have found a better way to explain.
Please don't follow me. I'll only be by the doorway.
I can still hear you from here if you need something.
I don't need anything right now. Take your minute properly.
I used to leave places before anyone could turn me down.
You can leave here because you want to. That's allowed.
I'm trying to work out whether I actually want to.
Then I should stop talking and let you do that.
There's something I could learn here, if we keep it small.
There is. But you can learn things in other places.
I know. I don't want you to be my only option.
You shouldn't. Keep looking if you need more paid hours.
Would that bother you, knowing I'm still looking somewhere else?
A little, probably. But that doesn't make it your problem.
Then I can offer one week, with the limits we discussed.
Are you sure that's an offer you want to make?
Yes. Not because you need saving. Because I want the work.
All right. Then I'll answer you as someone hiring you.
Five mornings, counting today. Six until nine, fifteen an hour.
Paid each morning. Any extra time gets agreed before it happens.
Two counter seats. Coffee and toast. I handle the hot things.
I handle cups and clearing. You teach me the rest gradually.
If I cancel, I call before you leave home for work.
By five fifteen, please. After that, I've already left home.
Five fifteen. I'll keep the number by the phone here.
If I can't come, I call then too, not just disappear.
After each morning, ten minutes to say what didn't work.
Inside the paid time. I don't want that sliding afterward.
Inside it. We stop serving early enough to finish by nine.
At the end, we decide whether another week makes sense.
Either of us can say no. We settle what's been worked.
And I don't lose today's pay if tomorrow doesn't happen.
You don't. I'm paying for work, not for keeping promises forever.
You don't have to guarantee the place will still be here.
I can't guarantee that. I can tell you what I know.
Tell me when it changes, before I'm standing outside again.
I will. I won't leave you reading another notice first.
Then I want the week. I don't need a bigger promise.
I'd like the week too. Even knowing it might not work.
We can find that out without pretending we've already solved it.
Agreed. We'll check the work, the hours, and the money.
All right. Tell me where you'd like me to start.
First, put that cup back. I can never find one.
The cup's already there. You're looking past it at me.
So it is. I'm going to have to get used to this.
Having the cups ready, or somebody telling you where they are?
Both, probably. Don't expect me to be graceful about it.
I wasn't. I'd like instructions more than graceful, to start.
The clean cloth stays here. The other one stays behind me.
And nothing hot on the lower shelf. I remember that.
Good. We'll check the two places before we open anything.
What time do you want to start serving this morning?
Seven. That gives us time to get the counter ready.
Then we should say seven, rather than let people guess.
I'll put the hours by the door before we serve.
Do you want the old notice put away for now?
Leave it folded on the back counter. Don't throw it out.
All right. We don't have to decide what happens afterward.
And if this feels wrong tomorrow, you'll tell me then?
Yes. Will you tell me, instead of printing another notice?
I'll tell you. Probably over coffee that actually has coffee in it.
I'd settle for knowing which mug you're putting mine in.
The one on your side. I can keep that much straight.
Good. I'll leave it there until you need the space.
There's a little note card by the register. Use that one.
Put it here on the counter, where we can see it.
